records.verbatim definition: Addresses used when a requirement is defined and is to be pointed to a process or a result. This relation may also be valid for example in a defined problem (Notes) or a point in time (Time).
records.normalized explanation: Points a Requirement, and in stated examples a Notes problem or Time item, to a Process or result.
records.source model-item type: Requirement; possibly Notes or Time Object depending on context
records.direction: Directed toward the process or result according to the wording pointed to; exact drawn arrow direction is not independently stated.
records.visual line or arrow form: Thin connector with arrowhead in the relationship overview; exact endpoint style is difficult to read.
records.connection meaning: Connects an addressing item to what it addresses.
records.context-dependent meaning: Meaning depends on whether the source is Requirement, Notes, or Time.
explicit restrictions: Do not generalize beyond the explicitly named contexts.

records.verbatim definition: Consists of used when we need to describe an organizational structure, product, process etc. (Inverse is ‘Is a part of’).
records.direction: Directed inverse of Is a part of.
records.visual line or arrow form: Connector shown in the relationship overview; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible.
records.connection meaning: States that the source consists of the target.
records.context-dependent meaning: May apply to organizational structure, product, process, etc.
explicit restrictions: Treat as inverse of Is a part of.
No cardinality is stated.

records.verbatim definition: Controls used in our flows when a prerequisite (Business Object) is directional for the process in question.
records.normalized explanation: Shows a prerequisite Business Object directing or controlling a Process.
records.direction: From prerequisite toward the process according to the flow wording and overview.
records.visual line or arrow form: Directed connector in flow context; exact line or arrow styling is not fully readable.
records.connection meaning: The prerequisite is directional for the Process.
records.context-dependent meaning: Meaning depends on the Business Object being a prerequisite.
explicit restrictions: Use in flows when the Business Object is a prerequisite with a directional role.

records.verbatim definition: Corresponds with used when we have two similar symbols that in fact are mirror image of each other (a result can correspond with a Class in a Class diagram).
records.normalized explanation: Links similar items that mirror one another across representations.
records.direction: Unresolved; wording does not explicitly establish one-way direction.
records.visual line or arrow form: Connector shown in overview; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible.
records.context-dependent meaning: Example: a result and a Class in a Class diagram.
explicit restrictions: Use for similar symbols that are mirror images of each other.

records.verbatim definition: Defines used to describe, for example, who defines a requirement or problem.
records.normalized explanation: Links a defining actor or item to a Requirement or problem.
records.direction: Directed from definer to defined item by ordinary wording; exact diagram direction is not fully legible.
records.visual line or arrow form: Connector shown in overview; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible.
records.connection meaning: Identifies who defines a Requirement or problem.
records.context-dependent meaning: The target can be a Requirement or a problem or Notes context.
explicit restrictions: The printed example does not establish an exhaustive source-type list.

records.verbatim definition: Flow used to describe the refinement flow and is drawn from prerequisites to the process and onwards to the process’s refinement result.
records.normalized explanation: Shows refinement movement from prerequisite Business Objects into a Process and onward to its result.
records.direction: Explicitly from prerequisites to Process and onward to refinement result.
records.visual line or arrow form: Directed flow arrows in the overview.
records.context-dependent meaning: Meaning depends on whether it enters the Process as a prerequisite or leaves it as a refinement result.
explicit restrictions: Use for refinement flow only as stated.
No token, sequence, or execution semantics are stated.

records.verbatim definition: Handles used for example to describe that a given Organization ‘Handles’ a certain product.
records.normalized explanation: Links an Organization to a product it handles.
records.direction: From Organization to handled product by sentence grammar; exact drawn direction is not fully legible.
records.visual line or arrow form: Connector shown in overview; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible.
records.connection meaning: States operational responsibility for handling a product.
records.context-dependent meaning: The example is Organization-to-product; broader use is not stated.
explicit restrictions: Do not infer ownership, custody, or lifecycle rules beyond Handles.

records.verbatim definition: Interrelates with used to describe an unspecified collaboration between two parts of our objects. This can be valid between two different interested parties or between two different processes, for example.
records.normalized explanation: Shows unspecified collaboration between two model items.
records.source model-item type: Model item, including Interested Party or Process
records.target model-item type: Model item, including Interested Party or Process
records.direction: Unresolved or likely non-directional, but not explicitly stated.
records.visual line or arrow form: Connector shown in overview; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible.
records.context-dependent meaning: Examples include Interested Party-to-Interested Party and Process-to-Process.
explicit restrictions: Use only when collaboration is intentionally unspecified.
Do not infer detailed exchange or control semantics.

records.verbatim definition: Is a part of used to describe ‘Is a part of’ structure (see the inverse, ‘Consists of’).
records.visual line or arrow form: Connector shown in overview; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible.
records.connection meaning: States that the source is part of the target.
records.context-dependent meaning: May apply to organizational structure, product, process, etc.
explicit restrictions: Treat as inverse of Consists of.
No cardinality is stated.

records.verbatim definition: Is a kind of used to describe category or relationship. A car is for example a type of vehicle. A fast order is a type of order. (Refer to the inverse ‘Is specialized in’).
records.normalized explanation: Describes specialization from a specific kind to a more general category.
records.direction: From specific kind to general category based on examples and inverse wording.
records.visual line or arrow form: Connector shown in overview; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible.
records.context-dependent meaning: Examples: car to vehicle; fast order to order.
explicit restrictions: Treat as inverse of Is specialized in.
No inheritance or software-class semantics are stated.

records.verbatim definition: Is specialized in used for describing categories or relationships. A vehicle can be specialized in a car. An order has its specialization in a fast order. (Compare the inverse ‘Is a kind of’).
records.normalized explanation: Describes specialization from a general category to a specific kind.
records.direction: From general category to specific kind based on examples and inverse wording.
records.visual line or arrow form: Connector shown in overview; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible.
records.connection meaning: States that the source has the target as a specialization.
records.context-dependent meaning: Examples: vehicle to car; order to fast order.
explicit restrictions: Treat as inverse of Is a kind of.
No inheritance or software-class semantics are stated.

records.verbatim definition: Is used by used in our flows when a prerequisite (Business Object) has a supporting role for the process in question.
records.normalized explanation: Shows a supporting prerequisite Business Object used by a Process.
records.direction: The official phrase is passive; relation is read as Business Object is used by Process.
records.visual line or arrow form: Directed connector in flow context; exact endpoint form is not fully readable.
records.context-dependent meaning: Meaning depends on the Business Object being a supporting prerequisite rather than a controlling one.
explicit restrictions: Use in flows when the prerequisite Business Object has a supporting role.

records.verbatim definition: Is situated at used to describe that an object is located in a specific place (Location).
records.normalized explanation: Links an object to a physical Location.
records.direction: From object to Location according to the phrase.
records.visual line or arrow form: Connector shown in the relationship overview; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible.
explicit restrictions: Use for location in a specific physical place.

records.verbatim definition: Is followed by used when we – by way of exception – describe how processes are laid in sequence without any intermediate result (Business Objects).
records.normalized explanation: Directly sequences Processes only as an exception when no intermediate Business Object is present.
records.direction: From earlier Process to following Process.
records.visual line or arrow form: Directed connector; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible in the overview.
records.context-dependent meaning: Used only when the normal intermediate result or Business Object is omitted.
explicit restrictions: Use by way of exception.
Only when processes are laid in sequence without an intermediate Business Object.

records.verbatim definition: Performs used to describe how a machine, resource or competence performs tasks in a process.
records.normalized explanation: Links a machine, resource, or competence to the Process tasks it performs.
records.direction: From performer to Process or task according to the phrase.
records.visual line or arrow form: Connector shown in overview; exact endpoint form is not reliably legible.
records.context-dependent meaning: Source type depends on whether the performer is a machine, resource, or competence.
explicit restrictions: No broader actor semantics or responsibility rules are stated.

records.verbatim definition: Secondary flow used in our flows where a result (Business Object) is a side effect of a task in the process in question.
records.normalized explanation: Shows a Business Object result that is a side effect of a Process task.
records.direction: From Process or task to side-effect result by the wording.
records.visual line or arrow form: Secondary directed flow in the overview; exact line distinction is not fully readable.
records.context-dependent meaning: Meaning depends on the result being a side effect rather than the principal refinement result.
explicit restrictions: Use only when the Business Object result is a side effect.

records.verbatim definition: Verification Flow used in our flows where a result (Business Object) creates verifying documentation for the process in question.
records.normalized explanation: Shows a Business Object result that provides verifying documentation for a Process.
records.source model-item type: Process or task or its result-producing context
records.direction: The wording is context-dependent; exact source-to-target arrow direction is not fully stated.
records.visual line or arrow form: Verification flow line in the overview; exact visual distinction is not fully readable.
records.context-dependent meaning: Meaning depends on the result serving as verification documentation for the Process.
explicit restrictions: Use only when the Business Object result creates verifying documentation.
